newsitem.title: USA: Madonna as mother - the next chapter.
newsitem.headline: Madonna as mother - the next chapter.

text.p: Now it's Madonna and child.

For a performer who relished her ability to shock and flout the rules with sexy songs, risque lyrics and outrageous antics, including an obscenity-laced national TV appearance with David Letterman, Madonna cherished a traditional role.
Now she's a mother, giving birth to a baby girl, Lourdes Maria, on Monday at a Los Angeles hospital.
Five years ago she was quoted as saying: "I long for children," but added she would only contemplate becoming a mother if she was sure the father would stick around.
She even said, half-jokingly, that she would advertise for a man to father her child.

Well that man turned out to be her personal physical trainer, Carlos Leon. Her publicist Liz Rosenberg said Madonna, 38, and Leon had been together for about a year and a half but were not married. She did not know if they had plans to marry but said "she's deliriously happy."
Her pregnancy was announced in April in Budapest where Madonna was filming the movie version of the musical "Evita" in which she plays the title role.

The singer's fame is founded on a string of hits but the notoriety that explains much of her runaway success rests unapologetically on raunch -- relentless bodily exposure and a celebratory invocation of sex in various forms.
Madonna Veronica Louise Ciccone had flings with several Hollywood stars, including Warren Beatty, and was married to actor/director Sean Penn.
Flamboyant basketball star Dennis Rodman also wrote in graphic detail about his affair with Madonna, sparking a host of late-night TV jokes about her sexual appetite for athletes.
In 1992, she published a photo album called "Sex," packed with pictures of herself acknowledging aspects of sexual behaviour including sado-masochism and lesbianism.
"Erotica," the record that followed, was laced with bedroom groaning and moaning.
Before these came "Truth or Dare" (titled "In Bed with Madonna" in Europe), a no-holds-barred documentary of the Michigan-born singer on tour.

On record, she loved to shock. She performed her first hit, the suggestive "Like a Virgin" as a pouting bride; "Material Girl" was a paean to empty materialism; "Papa Don't Preach" about teen pregnancy and the video of "Like a Prayer" upset the Catholic church with religious and sexual imagery.
For a woman who has been there and done that more than most, having a child could be the crown of a 12-year career.
Motherhood had eluded her, despite frequent media rumours that Madonna was pregnant and her conviction at one time that she was going to have a child with Penn.
She is the oldest of six children and was devoted to her mother, who died of breast cancer at 30.
Her first marriage in 1985 to Penn, nominated for an Oscar this year in "Dead Man Walking," was not a success.
"Shanghai Surprise," the movie they made together, was a box office disaster and the pair's stormy relationship caused them to be dubbed "the poison Penns" by the British tabloids.
Their 3-1/2 year marriage ended in January 1989.

Apart from the cult success of "Desperately Seeking Susan," and critical acclaim for her performance in "Dick Tracy," Madonna's film career has been disappointing, with a series of flops, including "Who's that Girl?" and "Body of Evidence."
There was also a disastrous attempt at stage acting in David Mamet's "Speed the Plough," in which she was mauled by the critics.
Madonna is hoping "Evita" gives her her first big-screen smash hit.
